title: Boggle's Brave Bridge
markdown:
In the gentle Hollowpeak Hills lived a little goblin named Boggle. His home was a cozy nook tucked among the roots of big trees. The air there always smelled like damp earth and wild flowers. Every day Boggle would step outside, his bright eyes wide with wonder. He loved to explore the quiet green hills and the whispering silver woods. His little goblin boots made soft thuds on the mossy paths, like tiny drums playing a peaceful song. He loved how the warm sunbeams played through the leaves, making pretty patterns on the forest floor. He loved the gentle hum of busy bees as they tumbled from one flower to another. But there was one small place, just past his favourite clover patch, that Boggle always tiptoed away from. A little bridge, no bigger than a fallen log, stretched over a softly murmuring stream. Though it never looked wobbly or weak, a whisper of worry would sometimes float into Boggle’s ears, making his shoulders pull up just a little.

Every single day Boggle would happily play among the ferns and wildflowers, his laughter like the tinkling of tiny bells. Yet his eyes would often look, just for a moment, toward that little bridge. A soft sigh would slip from his lips. He wished he could feel as sure as the wise old owl who hooted his calm words from the tallest pine tree. He wished he could feel as happy as the hares who leaped across the fields with joy. Most of all, he wanted to feel the same calm that came over him when he snuggled into his cozy goblin bed at night, wrapped in his softest blanket, listening to the quiet song of the wind.

Until one very special day, a new friend came to Boggle’s home and filled his world with even more warmth. A tiny kitten, no bigger than Boggle’s two hands held together. Her fur was as soft and pale as the first light of the moon on fresh snow. Boggle named her Silky. Silky’s purr was like a tiny warm rumble that vibrated through Boggle’s chest and made him feel peaceful and safe. Suddenly, as Silky curled up for a nap on his lap, purring a sleepy tune, Boggle had a brave thought. He decided he would take Silky for a walk in the moonlight through the little silver forest. And he would finally show himself that the tiny bridge was perfectly safe.

Because of that brave thought, Boggle, with Silky resting gently in his arms, began his moonlit walk. The silver forest sparkled all around them. The moonlight painted the leaves and the ground in shiny colours, as if the world had been sprinkled with moon dust. The air smelled wonderfully sweet, a mix of dewy petals that had just opened their faces to the night, and the warm earthy smell of the sleeping ground. Boggle hummed a little tune as he walked, a quiet song that seemed to float on the night air. Silky’s purr vibrated softly against his chest, a steady comforting sound.

As they came near the little stream where the tiny bridge lay, Boggle saw a warm light peeking through the trees. A little cottage, its windows glowing like friendly eyes. From it came the smell of freshly baked bread, warm and sweet. A kind face, with a dusting of flour, peeked out from the doorway. It was Cerys, the goblin baker, her smile as warm as her oven. “Well, hello there, young Boggle. And who is this lovely little moonbeam you have with you this fine evening?” Boggle, feeling shy but also sure of himself, told her about his plan to cross the little bridge with Silky. Cerys smiled a gentle smile. “Ah, the little bridge. It’s a perfectly safe little bridge, my dear boy. It has carried many a crumb and many a happy dream. It’s a friendly old bridge. Here,” she said, reaching into the cottage and offering Boggle a warm crumbly moon-muffin, “this will give you courage for your adventure. It’s made with starlight and bravery, just for moments like these.” Boggle took a bite of the muffin. It was warm, sweet, and tasted like a happy wish coming true.

Because of that kind offer and Cerys’s gentle words, Boggle looked down at Silky. She blinked her big gentle eyes at him and let out a tiny meow, as if to say she was ready. She seemed happy, not worried at all. Her tail gave a little flick. Boggle felt a flutter in his tummy, a familiar tickle of worry, but it felt much smaller now, like a moth’s wing brushing against him. He remembered Cerys’s words, the taste of the muffin, and the comforting rumble of Silky’s purr. He took a deep breath, the sweet night air filling his lungs with calm. He gently placed Silky on the grass near the edge of the bridge. She trotted toward it, her little tail held high like a proud flag.

Boggle watched her tiny paws step onto the wooden planks. Then, with a nod to himself, he followed. The moonlight sparkled on the flowing water below, a peaceful sound that whispered of quiet dreams. Boggle’s little boots made soft steady sounds on the wood. Each step felt more sure than the last. He looked over at Silky, who was sniffing a dandelion on the other side. Her purr was a happy hum that floated on the night air. Boggle’s heart felt light and joyful. The tiny bridge was indeed perfectly safe, a gentle path. And Silky was right there beside him, a soft warm purring friend. Everything felt just right.

Ever since then, Boggle still loved his cozy goblin bed, especially when moonbeams streamed through his window. He also walked to the clover patch without tiptoeing away. Sometimes he and Silky crossed the bridge just to see the dandelion on the other side. And as he looked up at the twinkling stars from his window, snuggled beside his beloved Silky, they drifted off to a peaceful happy slumber, filled with sweet dreams of moonlight, muffins, and a friendly old bridge that did not mind being crossed twice.
